lxc_2ad745396cea8be3.text: Memes do not spread because of one magic formula.

lxc_98b61f4b8dc12485.text: Learn how content, social influence, networks, attention, and algorithms interact—and why popularity is not evidence of truth.

lxc_15f797f6d676d0c6.text: Today, a meme often means a captioned image or video that people copy and change online.

lxc_4edd09ede17d4f6f.text: To understand why ideas go viral, we can start with The Selfish Gene (1976), where Richard Dawkins proposed “meme” as a name for a unit of cultural transmission: an idea, tune, fashion, or practice that passes from person to person.

lxc_43ee8d0cbcd69d83.text: His comparison with genes was powerful because it directed attention towards copying and survival.

lxc_7d1d0d3031303fc0.text: However, cultural information is not literally DNA.

lxc_8d33aed103ecf9d4.text: People can misunderstand it, combine it with other ideas, or deliberately redesign it.

lxc_cecdf4f97e845d61.text: Modern cultural-evolution research therefore treats the gene comparison as a useful starting point, not a complete explanation of culture.

lxc_0ccfc8f338949827.text: Cultural evolution can be described through three linked processes.

lxc_648e5ec63af8490b.text: Transmission happens when information moves between people through speech, imitation, writing, teaching, or media.

lxc_9b13d0c896f8ff84.text: Variation appears when the information changes, either by accident or by design.

lxc_1a59ce81b1fe4ee5.text: Selection happens when some versions are copied or remembered more than others.

lxc_880c8551d9c9a5db.text: Here, “selected” does not mean morally good, factually true, or biologically superior.

lxc_179924eb98a8abe4.text: It only means that one version became more common or lasted longer in a particular environment.

lxc_837206217916b1b2.text: A joke may become shorter because short versions are easier to retell.

lxc_4cceb494a9c14331.text: A recipe may become more detailed because accuracy matters to the cooks using it.

lxc_3e8f7e2dcf7aa345.text: People may notice content because it is surprising, useful, frightening, funny, or easy to remember.

lxc_bc438d0ee9f1c2cc.text: They may also copy a person who seems respected or successful.

lxc_f6d0ed532507b9fa.text: In one narrative experiment, both the content of a story and the supposed prestige of its source influenced transmission; prestige mattered, but several content effects were stronger.

lxc_d9c12ccef43ce206.text: Social information can then create a feedback loop.

lxc_b63723021e1fb730.text: In a controlled online music experiment, 14,341 people chose songs by unknown bands.

lxc_a162adf505b965d1.text: When participants could see earlier download numbers, popular songs became more unequal and final rankings became less predictable.

lxc_cb22507d460bb7b3.text: Quality still had some influence, but early popularity helped create later popularity.

lxc_dcd0e5ee6078900a.text: A transmission test asks, “Will people pass this on?”

lxc_ce22c07402da213d.text: A truth test asks, “Is the claim supported by reliable evidence?”

lxc_c6fd99b0f61644e2.text: These tests can produce different answers.

lxc_d9d81886eeef8b7b.text: A large study followed about 126,000 stories shared on Twitter from 2006 to 2017 and used six fact-checking organizations to classify them.

lxc_77761e8eadc9660f.text: In that dataset, false stories travelled farther, faster, deeper, and more broadly than true stories.

lxc_27641627ee4c473f.text: The researchers also found that false news tended to be more novel.

lxc_d9a49d923a373a9b.text: This does not prove that every false claim beats every true one, or that the same pattern exists on every platform.

lxc_68860e05da521684.text: It shows why share counts cannot replace evidence.

lxc_2f0d0835bc5e9a44.text: People often use “viral” to mean “very popular,” but network scientists can ask a more precise question: what shape did the spread take?

lxc_9cc0f225ec35c4be.text: Imagine two messages with one million views.

lxc_0a0dfaee2782439f.text: A celebrity sends the first directly to a huge audience, creating a broadcast shaped like a star.

lxc_1e3e850ee1ce246d.text: The second passes through many generations: one person shares it, several recipients share it again, and new branches continue.

lxc_b590a2d974f97d39.text: Researchers call this second quality structural virality.

lxc_8648affe0311f505.text: After examining one billion diffusion events on Twitter, they found that popular events had many different shapes.

lxc_cffedf11abcc4927.text: However, structural virality was usually low, and a large broadcast often produced most of the popularity.

lxc_76d0aecc6f93eefb.text: Reach and person-to-person depth are not the same measurement.

lxc_a4579a2aeeafd5f2.text: The language of contagion is another model, not a claim that ideas are diseases.

lxc_a5a7c9f83744565d.text: In a simple contagion, one contact may be enough to transmit information, as when you learn that a concert exists.

lxc_2cd6877f71ade540.text: A complex contagion requires reinforcement from several people before someone adopts a risky, costly, or uncertain behavior.

lxc_b882ce187a1636ad.text: Joining a protest, using an unfamiliar technology, or accepting a new group rule may work this way.

lxc_af096c5130fb0349.text: In a randomized online experiment with 1,528 participants, a health behavior spread farther and faster through clustered networks than through random networks.

lxc_6db5a0e3b35a1e40.text: The result does not mean clustering always wins; it shows that the kind of decision changes which network structure is useful.

lxc_0da2b0d73bd30ec0.text: A network is a pattern of connections between people or groups.

lxc_7c542024cc74b3c3.text: Dense clusters create repeated contact, shared expectations, and trust, so they can support complex adoption.

lxc_cef6239cb8386055.text: Bridges connect different clusters and carry information into new communities.

lxc_10ad6411684a92dd.text: Yet one weak bridge may deliver a message without providing enough reinforcement for action.

lxc_bf6355b5f69efea8.text: Complex-contagion theory therefore highlights bridge width: several independent links between groups may matter more than one long connection.

lxc_029599306b1a3c1a.text: There is no universally perfect network.

lxc_2f6544ceb960f893.text: Tight clusters can strengthen support but also trap an idea inside one group.

lxc_48db536907c618b8.text: Numerous bridges can increase reach but may weaken repeated confirmation.

lxc_b7bee6483d295c81.text: The outcome depends on what is spreading and what adoption requires.

lxc_c0a2933ecca00b0d.text: People cannot inspect every message they receive.

lxc_c1d13f167628af54.text: In one agent-based model, limited attention and network structure produced large differences in meme popularity even when the modeled items had equal quality.

lxc_da6d00b19b10ecca.text: This does not prove that real ideas are equal; it reveals how competition for attention can magnify small accidents.

lxc_ff2e2e3f25720906.text: Platforms add another layer by ranking what users see.

lxc_a3145c610409ba78.text: A large randomized Twitter experiment found that an algorithmic timeline changed the relative visibility of political content compared with a reverse-chronological feed.

lxc_73d44a1ad7596080.text: Content matters too: in selected political discussions, moral-emotional language was associated with more sharing, especially inside ideological groups.

lxc_6a2b6b149df5e42d.text: That finding was observational, so it is not a universal recipe.

lxc_250365041f135514.text: Algorithms, human choices, and content interact in feedback loops.

lxc_85c8895aa49eb77c.text: No single feature explains why an idea takes over.

lxc_57205666ce99afe4.text: A better analysis uses six layers.

lxc_766a5257cd360584.text: Content asks what the message says and how memorable it is.

lxc_9bbedcd4bd4c7079.text: Mind asks what emotions, knowledge, and goals people bring.

lxc_c8f57fc64f08a72b.text: Source asks who communicates it and what social signals surround that person.

lxc_4e73d2adc4315f11.text: Network asks how groups, clusters, and bridges are arranged.

lxc_fb96a2dfe46e977f.text: Time asks whether events and early accidents create an opportunity.

lxc_f7da7304e87c1882.text: Platform asks how interfaces and ranking distribute attention.

lxc_83a1c432a3d7fa31.text: These layers can also guide responsible communication.

lxc_e58590dedea765f7.text: Make accurate information clear and easy to pass on, but keep the evidence attached.

lxc_b60eb72e664c9074.text: Build trusted connections across groups, but do not manufacture false popularity.

lxc_956536babf365516.text: The aim is not merely to win attention; it is to help valuable ideas travel without sacrificing truth.
